decision: One pull request makes price-watcher safe to show. Scrub personal data, make checks idempotent, add behavior tests, prove a local run, and replace the README.
why: The repo stays private and history is not rewritten. The smallest change is reliability and cleanup, not a new product.

decision: Removed the stale plan, unused packages, boilerplate icons, the personal Gmail default, and the home-directory path in the check script.
why: Dead weight and personal data should not ship in a portfolio copy. History is not rewritten.
result: personal email gone from the tree

decision: A repeated check stores one observation and sends one alert per price. One thrown product does not stop the run. Env email and browser channel are checked before scraping.
why: Re-running a scheduled check must not duplicate rows or spam alerts.

decision: Tracked a local product page in headless Chromium. Price went from 48 to 36 dollars, the chart updated, the alert was logged, and a third check said unchanged.
why: books.toscrape.com loaded but its price is in pounds with no JSON-LD, so the proof uses a local page.

decision: Left the Duluth name matcher, the password-in-cookie gate, and the Next middleware filename.
why: Those are real limits, and changing them is a new design, not a cleanup.

decision: An alert is once per price, including a price you already alerted on and then left. A failed send at that price is still retried.
why: The first version only looked at the latest alert, so 36 then 30 then 36 sent a second email for 36.

decision: A failed percentage-drop email is retried even after the stored price has moved. A dry run counts as sent for that price.
why: The first retry only worked for a target price, because a repeat check compared the price with itself.

decision: Recaptured the dashboard after the chart animation was turned off, so the line runs from 48 dollars to 36.
why: The earlier screenshot was taken while the chart was still drawing.
result: third check unchanged, email not sent

decision: The login cookie is an HMAC of a fixed payload and an expiry, checked with a constant-time compare. The gate file is src/proxy.ts.
why: A reviewer will read the auth code, and the raw password must not sit in the cookie. The build warned on the old middleware filename.
result: 27 tests passed, build has no middleware warning, browser login reached the dashboard
